modelResponse.episodeSummary: Robert D. Hale, Ventricular Fibrillation, critical, pulseless/hemodynamically unstable
keyECGEvidence: morphology: No organized QRS; coarse fibrillatory waves ~5 Hz
stDeviationMm: ST elevation 4 mm V2–V4 on rhythm strip 90 s pre-arrest
preEventNote: Runs of PVCs then R-on-T preceded onset; 12-lead 8 min prior showed anterior ST elevation
modelResponse.mechanism: Myocardial ischemia leading to electrical instability and R-on-T phenomenon, triggering ventricular fibrillation
contributingFactors: History of coronary artery disease and prior anterior MI

rejectedAlternatives.why: Potassium 4.1 mmol/L and Magnesium 2.0 mg/dL are within normal reference ranges.
No evidence of digoxin administration in medications or toxic serum levels provided.
Presence of anterior ST elevation 4 mm V2–V4 and critical troponin elevation strongly points to primary cardiac ischemia over pulmonary etiology.

recommendedActions: Initiate high-quality CPR and airway management per ACLS guidelines
Administer Amiodarone or Lidocaine for refractory VF
STOP Nitroglycerin IV infusion (due to hypotension/pulseless state)
Prepare for emergent Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) upon ROSC
